# Add this to ~/.claude/settings.json (merge into an existing "hooks" block).
# Then run `claude` inside a `roost` window and its badge tracks its state.
# Outside roost these hooks are silent no-ops.
# PermissionRequest is what paints the red, and it fires as the dialog opens.
# Measured on Claude Code 2.1.278: 11-16 ms after the dialog appears, where the
# permission_prompt Notification below arrives a flat 6.00 s after it — and a
# dialog answered inside those six seconds fires no Notification at all, so it
# was never painted and `roost send` typed into it. The hook prints nothing and
# decides nothing: an `allow` or a `deny` on this event would answer the dialog
# on your behalf, and roost never does that.
# "matcher": "permission_prompt" matters on the Notification entry — an
# unmatched Notification hook also fires for idle_prompt/auth_success, which
# would paint a finished agent red. That entry stays as the fallback for a
# Claude too old for PermissionRequest; on a current one it only moves the
# stamp for a dialog that is still open.
# PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure are what clear the red: no hook fires when
# you answer a permission dialog, so without them the window stays blocked
# until the whole turn ends. BOTH are needed — PostToolUse fires only when the
# tool SUCCEEDS, so a command that exits non-zero after you said Yes would
# otherwise leave the window red for the rest of the turn.
# --notification-hook on the Notification entry, and
# --permission-request-hook on the PermissionRequest entry, are what clear the
# red after "No" or Esc, when no hook fires at all: they record the payload's
# transcript_path, and `roost send`, `read` and `wait-done` read Claude's own
# transcript to prove the dialog was declined. Leave them off and a declined
# dialog keeps its red until your next prompt.
# --stop-hook on the Stop entry is what powers `roost read`: it lets the hook
# read Stop's JSON payload, whose last_assistant_message field carries the
# turn's reply. Leave it off and everything still badges correctly — `roost
# read` just falls back to scraping the pane's screen, and tells you it did.
# StopFailure is what ends a turn that FAILED — a rate limit, an overload, a
# model that does not exist. Claude fires it instead of Stop and nothing after
# it, so without it the badge stays working on an agent that has stopped. It
# badges error, and --stop-failure-hook records which kind of API error for
# `roost wait-done` and `read` to print. It has no matcher on purpose: every
# kind Claude reports is a turn that did not finish.
#
# SessionStart is the odd one out: the other seven report state OUTWARD, and it
# is the only one that feeds context IN. It tells the agent it is inside roost
# and gives it its own pane id, so it reaches for `roost split` rather than a
# bare `tmux split-window` that would target the user's ordinary tmux server.
#
# Its "matcher": "*" is a deliberate choice, not a default. SessionStart fires
# for five sources — startup, resume, clear, compact and fork — and NONE of
# them leaves the preamble in place: startup and fork have no context yet,
# /clear wipes it, and compact replaces it with a summary that drops it. So all
# five need the injection, and naming a subset would also silently skip
# whichever source Claude Code adds next. The cost of the one case that is
# arguably redundant (resume, where the original injection may still be in the
# transcript) is a few duplicated lines; the cost of missing one is an agent
# that has forgotten which server it is on.
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "matcher": "*",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-session-context" } ] }
    ],
    "UserPromptSubmit": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state working" } ] }
    ],
    "PermissionRequest": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state blocked --permission-request-hook" } ] }
    ],
    "Notification": [
      { "matcher": "permission_prompt",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state blocked --notification-hook" } ] }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state working" } ] }
    ],
    "PostToolUseFailure": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state working" } ] }
    ],
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state done --stop-hook" } ] }
    ],
    "StopFailure": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/scripts/roost-agent-state error --stop-failure-hook" } ] }
    ]
  }
}
